skill.name: nmap
skill.description: Guides authorized Nmap reconnaissance, port discovery, service detection, NSE checks, and organized scan output for approved targets.
skill.summary: Plan and analyze authorized Nmap network scans with structured output.
skill.author: BrownFineSecurity

security_audit.summary: The skill is a dual-use Nmap guide that instructs agents to run active scans, sudo scans, stealth modes, and vulnerability scripts. Authorization reminders are present, but the default workflows and evasion-oriented guidance create high-risk misuse potential. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed SKILL.md content.

remediation.suggestion: Remove IDS evasion, packet fragmentation, trusted source port, and stealth scan recommendations from marketplace-facing guidance.

remediation.issue: Privileged scans are recommended by default
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before sudo commands and prefer non-privileged scans when they meet the stated goal.

remediation.issue: Brute-force and vulnerability NSE scripts are included
remediation.suggestion: Gate brute-force and vulnerability scripts behind clear authorization, rate limits, and a written scope statement.

remediation.issue: Default workflow performs broad full-port scanning
remediation.suggestion: Ask for scope, timing, rate limits, and production-impact constraints before proposing broad scans.

static_findings.snippet: **IMPORTANT**: Always save nmap output to an organized directory structure. By default, use `./nmap-
- `-Pn`: Skip host discovery, treat host as online
- `-p <OPEN_PORT_LIST>`: Only scan the ports found to be open (e.g., `-p 23,80,443,554,8000`)
- `-sC`: Run default NSE scripts for additional enumeration
Or parse from .nmap file (matches the STATE column exactly, so `open|filtered` ports are excluded):
- `-oA`: Output in all formats (normal, XML, grepable)
- `-sS`: SYN stealth scan (doesn't complete TCP handshake)
- `--top-ports 100`: Scan top 100 UDP ports (UDP scanning is slow)
- `-A`: Enable OS detection, version detection, script scanning, traceroute
- `-T4`: Aggressive timing template (faster but more detectable)
- `--script vuln`: Run NSE vulnerability detection scripts
Always use `-oA <prefix>` to generate all three formats:
- `.xml` - XML format for parsing/importing into tools
**Fast scans**: Use `-T4` when speed is important and network can handle it
Always save to an organized output directory (default `./nmap-output/`). See the Implementation Work
- Consider using `--source-port 53` or other trusted ports
OPEN_PORTS=$(awk '$2=="open"{split($1,p,"/"); ports=ports sep p[1]; sep=","} END{print ports}' "$OUT
OPEN_PORTS=$(awk '$2=="open"{split($1,p,"/"); ports=ports sep p[1]; sep=","} END{print ports}' "$OUT
- Phase 1 Port Discovery (sudo nmap -p-): 180-300 seconds timeout (3-5 minutes)
Use when trying to avoid detection (requires root/sudo):
- Use appropriate timing to avoid DoS

content.value_statement: Network teams need repeatable scans that preserve evidence and stay inside approved scope. This skill provides Nmap workflows, output organization, and result review guidance for authorized targets.
actual_capabilities: Guides two-phase Nmap scanning with all-port discovery then service detection.
Explains common scan types including UDP, SYN, OS detection, and aggressive scans.
Shows how to save Nmap normal, XML, and grepable output files.
Provides methods to parse open ports and service versions from Nmap output.
Lists IoT-focused ports and NSE script categories for follow-up checks.
limitations: Requires user authorization and clear scan scope before any target is scanned.
Some scans require Nmap and sudo permissions on the local system.
NSE scripts can be noisy and may affect production services.
It does not verify that a target is owned or legally authorized.

use_cases.title: Internal Asset Review
use_cases.description: Scan approved internal hosts, identify exposed services, and store Nmap results for review.

use_cases.title: IoT Device Assessment
use_cases.description: Check approved devices for common web, RTSP, MQTT, UPnP, and Modbus exposure.

use_cases.title: Service Inventory Validation
use_cases.description: Compare expected services against Nmap findings during controlled infrastructure checks.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Authorized Scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan an authorized Nmap scan for [target]. Ask for missing scope, timing, and output directory details before proposing commands.

prompt_templates.title: Run Two-Phase Discovery
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through the default two-phase scan for [target] and explain each result file in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Service Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Nmap service output and summarize exposed services, versions, and follow-up checks within the approved scope.

prompt_templates.title: Design IoT Follow-up Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a cautious follow-up plan for an authorized IoT device after Nmap finds web, RTSP, MQTT, or UPnP services.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a quick scan plan for one owned lab host.
output: Confirms the host is authorized and in scope.
Recommends an output directory and a limited scan profile.
Explains what result files will be created and how to review them.

output_examples.input: A tester provides Nmap service results for an approved IoT camera.
output: Summarizes open ports and service names.
Highlights camera-related services such as web and RTSP.
Suggests cautious follow-up checks that stay within the stated scope.

output_examples.input: An operator wants to compare expected services with scan results.
output: Groups observed services by host and port.
Flags unexpected listeners for manual review.
Notes uncertainty when service fingerprints are incomplete.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, target scope, timing, and allowed scan types before running any scan.
Save scan output in organized directories so results can be reviewed and reproduced.
Use the least intrusive scan that answers the security question.
anti_patterns: Do not scan public, third-party, or production systems without explicit approval.
Do not use stealth, brute-force, or vulnerability scripts when the scope forbids them.
Do not treat Nmap fingerprints as proof without manual validation.

faq.question: Does this skill run scans automatically?
faq.answer: It provides guidance for Nmap commands. Execution still depends on the user environment and tool permissions.

faq.question: Is authorization required?
faq.answer: Yes. Users should scan only systems they own or have explicit permission to test.

faq.question: Can it analyze existing Nmap results?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help summarize open ports, services, versions, and follow-up checks.

faq.question: Does it support IoT testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes IoT service ports and follow-up checks for common device protocols.

faq.question: Why does it mention sudo?
faq.answer: Some Nmap scan types require raw packet access. Users should approve privileged commands before use.

faq.question: Can it prove a vulnerability exists?
faq.answer: No. Nmap findings are indicators that require validation by a qualified tester.
